newsitem.title: USA: Plaintiffs seek ouster of judge in implant case.
newsitem.headline: Plaintiffs seek ouster of judge in implant case.

text.p: A federal judge who handed a major legal setback to woman suing breast-implant manufacturers should be removed from the case because his own wife has had implants, plaintiffs' lawyers said.

Attorneys for Susan McAleer, who is suing Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. over illness she contends was caused by her breast implant, filed a motion this week seeking to remove U.S. District Judge Robert Jones from the case.
Jones set a precedent last month when he ruled there was not sufficient scientific evidence to prove silicone-gel breast implants cause disease.
In a transcript of a Dec. 20 hearing attached to the motion, Jones said efforts to use his wife's "personal tragedy" to attack his decision were "sleazy."
In that hearing, he volunteered that his wife, Pearl, had two breast implants, one in 1977 and another in 1978.

He said she had trouble with the first implant, but a later one has been adequate, though "not anywhere any cosmetic perfection." He said she has since counselled many women who have had mastectomies.

McAleer is one of 70 Oregon women who have filed lawsuits over breast implants made by Baxter Healthcare Co., Baxter International Inc., Bristol-Myers Squibb, Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Co. and Dow Corning Corp.
The largest manufacturer, Dow Corning, a joint venture between Dow Chemical Co. and Corning Inc., filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in May 1995.
U.S. District Judge Ancer Haggerty will rule on the conflict-of-interest motion.
